en.greeting: Hi! Today you learn to build new words from words you already know, and to pick the right form for a sentence.

steps.title: Prefixes change the meaning
steps.text: Let's start at the front of the word.
steps.body:
A **prefix** is a small piece at the **front** of a word. It changes the meaning, but the kind of word stays the same.
- **un-** = not: *unhappy, unusual, unemployed*
- **dis-** = not / the opposite: *dishonest, disagree, dislike*
- **re-** = again: *redo, rewrite, rebuild*
Indonesian writes *tidak jujur* as two words; English joins the 'not' to the word: *dishonest*.

steps.title: un- or dis-?
steps.text: Read these sentences out loud.
steps.body: **There's no rule** for un- or dis-: learn each word with its prefix. That's why 'unhonest' is wrong: the word is **dishonest**. If you must guess, un- is more common, but check a dictionary. Not every 're' word is re + word: *remember* and *report* aren't 'again'. Note: **in-/im-** also mean not: *incorrect, impossible*.

examples.en: Sari was unhappy with her old job.
examples.id: Sari tidak senang dengan pekerjaan lamanya.

examples.en: My cousin is unemployed. He's looking for a job.
examples.id: Sepupu saya menganggur. Dia sedang mencari kerja.

examples.en: I dislike working on Saturdays.
examples.id: Saya tidak suka kerja di hari Sabtu.

examples.en: My wallet disappeared on the KRL this morning.
examples.id: Dompet saya hilang di KRL tadi pagi.

examples.en: My manager didn't like the slides, so I had to redo them.
examples.id: Atasan saya tidak suka slide-nya, jadi saya harus membuatnya ulang.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Choose the right word.

question.prompt: Don't trust that seller. He's ___: the phone he sold me was fake.
question.explanation: **honest** takes **dis-**: *dishonest*. There's no rule for un- or dis-, so 'unhonest' sounds logical but isn't a word. 'inhonest' doesn't exist either.

steps.title: Suffixes: people and things
steps.text: Now the end of the word.
steps.body:
A **suffix** is a piece at the **end**. It usually changes the kind of word.
- **-er / -or** = the person doing it: *teacher, manager, visitor*. Most take -er; learn the -or ones. -er can be a machine too: *charger*.
- **-tion / -sion** and **-ment** make a **noun** (a thing word) from a verb: *inform → information, decide → decision, pay → payment, develop → development*.
Watch the spelling: *explain → explanation* (no i). Like Indonesian *bayar → pembayaran*.

steps.title: -ful and -less
steps.text: Two endings that make describing words.
steps.body: **-ful** = with, full of; **-less** = without: *useful / useless, careful / careless* (ceroboh), *helpful, cashless*. The suffix **-ful** has **one l**; add -ly for an adverb and you get two: *carefully*. Not every -ful word has a -less partner: *beautiful*, and *successful → unsuccessful*.

examples.en: This app is really helpful for learning new words.
examples.id: Aplikasi ini sangat membantu untuk belajar kata baru.

examples.en: Be careful! The floor is wet.
examples.id: Hati-hati! Lantainya basah.

examples.en: I made a careless mistake in the email.
examples.id: Saya membuat kesalahan karena ceroboh di email itu.

examples.en: More and more shops in Jakarta are cashless.
examples.id: Semakin banyak toko di Jakarta yang nontunai.

examples.en: Please drive carefully.
examples.id: Tolong menyetir dengan hati-hati.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pick the right word.

question.prompt: This map app is really ___. It always shows me the fastest way to the office.
question.explanation: The app helps, so it's **useful** (-ful = with: it has a use). **useless** means the opposite, and 'usefull' has one l too many: the suffix is **-ful**.

steps.title: Word families
steps.text: Now the key skill: choosing the right form.
steps.body:
Words come in families: *decide / decision / decisive*, *succeed / success / successful / successfully*, *employ / employer / employee*. Look around the gap:
- after **a / the / my** (nothing after) → **noun**: *a decision*
- after **be** or **very**, or **before a noun** → **adjective**: *very successful, a successful shop*
- after a **verb** (saying how) → **adverb**: *finished successfully*
- after **to / can / don't** → **verb**: *I can't decide*
Indonesian does this too: *memutuskan, keputusan*.

steps.title: Which form?
steps.text: Look at the word before or after each family word.
steps.body: *my* + noun (decision), *can't* + verb (decide), *a* + adjective + noun (successful shop), verb + object + adverb (passed her test successfully). **employer** gives the job; **employee** (em-ploy-EE) does it.

examples.en: It's my decision, not yours.
examples.id: Itu keputusan saya, bukan keputusanmu.

examples.en: I can't decide. Can you help me?
examples.id: Saya tidak bisa memutuskan. Bisa bantu saya?

examples.en: My brother runs a successful online shop.
examples.id: Kakak saya punya toko online yang sukses.

examples.en: Rina passed her driving test successfully.
examples.id: Rina lulus ujian menyetirnya dengan sukses.

examples.en: The factory has five hundred employees.
examples.id: Pabrik itu punya lima ratus karyawan.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Which form fits the gap?

question.prompt: Rina's warung is always full of customers. Her business is very ___.
question.explanation: After **is very** you need an **adjective**: *successful*. *success* is a noun ('very success' is a common mistake), and *successfully* is an adverb for how someone does something.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Describe Pak Hasan.

question.solution: Pak Hasan is a very decisive manager.
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Pak Hasan manajer yang sangat tegas.
question.explanation: *decisive* (tegas) is the adjective of *decide*. An adjective goes **before the noun**: *a very decisive manager*, not 'a manager very decisive' (Indonesian puts it after: *manajer yang tegas*).

steps.title: Prefix mengubah arti
steps.text: Kita mulai dari depan kata.
steps.body:
**Prefix** (awalan) adalah potongan kecil di **depan** kata. Prefix mengubah arti, tapi jenis katanya tetap.
- **un-** = tidak: *unhappy, unusual, unemployed* (menganggur)
- **dis-** = tidak / kebalikannya: *dishonest, disagree, dislike*
- **re-** = lagi, ulang: *redo, rewrite, rebuild*
Bahasa Indonesia menulis *tidak jujur* dua kata; bahasa Inggris menggabungkan 'tidak' ke katanya: *dishonest*.

steps.title: un- atau dis-?
steps.text: Baca kalimat-kalimat ini dengan suara keras.
steps.body: **Tidak ada aturan** untuk un- atau dis-: hafalkan setiap kata bersama prefix-nya. Karena itu 'unhonest' salah: katanya **dishonest**. Kalau harus menebak, un- lebih sering dipakai, tapi cek kamus. Tidak semua kata 're' itu re + kata: *remember* dan *report* tidak berarti 'lagi'. Catatan: **in-/im-** juga berarti tidak: *incorrect, impossible*.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pilih kata yang benar.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Don't trust that seller. He's ___: the phone he sold me was fake.
question.explanation: **honest** memakai **dis-**: *dishonest* (tidak jujur). Tidak ada aturan untuk un- atau dis-, jadi 'unhonest' kedengarannya logis tapi bukan kata bahasa Inggris. 'inhonest' juga tidak ada.

steps.title: Suffix: orang dan benda
steps.text: Sekarang bagian belakang kata.
steps.body:
**Suffix** (akhiran) adalah potongan di **belakang** kata. Biasanya suffix mengubah jenis kata.
- **-er / -or** = orang yang melakukannya: *teacher, manager, visitor*. Kebanyakan pakai -er; yang -or dihafal. -er juga bisa alat: *charger*.
- **-tion / -sion** dan **-ment** membuat **kata benda** dari kata kerja: *inform → information, decide → decision, pay → payment, develop → development*.
Perhatikan ejaannya: *explain → explanation* (tanpa i). Mirip *bayar → pembayaran*.

steps.title: -ful dan -less
steps.text: Dua akhiran yang membuat kata sifat.
steps.body: **-ful** = dengan, penuh; **-less** = tanpa: *useful / useless, careful / careless* (ceroboh), *helpful, cashless* (nontunai). Akhiran **-ful** pakai **satu l**; tambah -ly untuk adverb dan jadi dua: *carefully*. Tidak semua kata -ful punya pasangan -less: *beautiful*, dan *successful → unsuccessful*.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pilih kata yang tepat.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: This map app is really ___. It always shows me the fastest way to the office.
question.explanation: Aplikasinya membantu, jadi **useful** (berguna; -ful = dengan). **useless** artinya kebalikannya, dan 'usefull' kelebihan satu l: akhirannya **-ful**.

steps.title: Keluarga kata
steps.text: Sekarang keterampilan kuncinya: memilih bentuk yang tepat.
steps.body:
Kata punya keluarga: *decide / decision / decisive*, *succeed / success / successful / successfully*, *employ / employer / employee*. Lihat sekitar titik-titiknya:
- setelah **a / the / my** (tanpa kata sesudahnya) → **kata benda**: *a decision*
- setelah **be** atau **very**, atau **sebelum kata benda** → **kata sifat**: *very successful, a successful shop*
- setelah **kata kerja** (menjelaskan bagaimana) → **adverb**: *finished successfully*
- setelah **to / can / don't** → **kata kerja**: *I can't decide*
Bahasa Indonesia juga begitu: *memutuskan, keputusan*.

steps.title: Bentuk yang mana?
steps.text: Perhatikan kata sebelum atau sesudah setiap kata dari keluarga itu.
steps.body: *my* + kata benda (decision), *can't* + kata kerja (decide), *a* + kata sifat + kata benda (successful shop), kata kerja + objek + adverb (passed her test successfully). **employer** memberi pekerjaan; **employee** (em-ploy-II) yang bekerja.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bentuk mana yang cocok?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Rina's warung is always full of customers. Her business is very ___.
question.explanation: Setelah **is very** kamu butuh **kata sifat**: *successful*. *success* adalah kata benda ('very success' kesalahan yang sering terjadi), dan *successfully* adalah adverb untuk bagaimana seseorang melakukan sesuatu.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Gambarkan Pak Hasan.

question.solution: Pak Hasan is a very decisive manager.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Pak Hasan manajer yang sangat tegas.
question.explanation: *decisive* (tegas) adalah kata sifat dari *decide*. Kata sifat ada **sebelum kata benda**: *a very decisive manager*, bukan 'a manager very decisive' (bahasa Indonesia menaruhnya di belakang: *manajer yang tegas*).
